extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or graduate students in mathematics (functional analysis / measure theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and states the definitions, propositions, and theorems about regular Borel (signed and complex) measures, total variation, the correspondence between measures and continuous linear functionals (Riesz representation), and basic Banach/Hilbert space facts. Targets the measure-theoretic underpinning of duals of C(X) and basic Banach-space examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition of continuous linear functional into positive linear functionals (Proposition 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be a compact Hausdorff space and ` a continuous linear functional on C(X). If ` takes real values on real-valued functions then define `+ and `− by appropriate sup/inf formulas; `+ and `− extend to positive linear functionals on C(X) with ` = `+ − `−. If ` does not necessarily take real values on real-valued functions, then ` is a complex linear combination of positive linear functionals on C(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: `+` and `−` are constructed by taking suprema over continuous functions g with 0 ≤ g ≤ f (and related formulas). The proposition reduces the complex-valued case to the real-valued case by expressing ` as combinations of functionals that take real values on real functions; then apply Theorem 11.1 to represent the positive functionals as integrations against regular Borel measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed measure and Jordan decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: A real-valued completely additive set function ρ on a σ-algebra is called a signed measure. If bounded (sup_E |ρ(E)| < ∞) then by Theorem 9.14 it has a Jordan decomposition ρ = ρ+ − ρ− with ρ+ and ρ− uniquely determined finite measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the Borel sets of a compact Hausdorff space, ρ is a regular Borel signed measure if its Jordan decomposition is into regular Borel measures. If any decomposition of a bounded signed measure as difference of regular Borel measures satisfies ρ+ ≤ ∫+ and ρ− ≤ ∫−, uniqueness and Proposition 11.20 force the components to be regular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular Borel signed measures form a real vector space M(X, R)
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection of regular Borel signed measures on X is a real vector space M(X, R); sums and scalar multiples of regular Borel signed measures are regular (closed under vector-space operations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closure under addition follows by combining Jordan decompositions: sums of regular (nonnegative) measures are regular, and the algebraic manipulations on decompositions show the sum of signed measures is regular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norm on M(X, R) via Jordan decomposition (Proposition 11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ρ in M(X, R) with Jordan decomposition ρ = ρ+ − ρ−, define the norm ||ρ|| = ρ+(X) + ρ−(X). This turns M(X, R) into a real normed linear space with the stated norm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs establish the triangle inequality and homogeneity using properties of Jordan decompositions and comparisons of positive/negative parts under addition and scalar multiplication; equality and scaling behavior are discussed (e.g., ||cρ|| = |c| ||ρ||).

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-case Riesz correspondence is isometric (Theorem 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The real-linear map of M(X, R) onto C(X, R)* given by ρ ↦ (f ↦ ∫ f dρ) is one-to-one and norm preserving: the measure norm equals the operator norm on the corresponding continuous linear functional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The norm of a functional ` is the least constant C with |`(f)| ≤ C ||f||_sup for all f. Proof that the map is one-one uses uniqueness of Jordan decomposition; to show isometry use Hahn decomposition, regularity, Urysohn's Lemma to build test functions f with ||f||_sup = 1 approximating the positive/negative parts and derive the norm equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex regular Borel measures: decomposition into real and imaginary parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A regular Borel complex measure ρ on compact X is an expression ρ = ρR + i ρI where ρR and ρI are regular Borel signed measures. The space M(X, C) of such measures is a complex vector space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces complex measures to pairs of regular signed measures; Proposition 11.24 and the real-case results extend to the complex-linear map into C(X, C)* via integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total variation measure and total-variation norm (definition and Proposition 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ρ in M(X, C) define the total-variation set function |ρ|(E) as the supremum of Σ |ρ(E_j)| over all finite collections of disjoint Borel sets {E_j} ⊆ E. The total-variation norm is ||ρ|| = |ρ|(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 11.27: |ρ| is a regular Borel measure, the total-variation norm makes M(X, C) into a normed linear space; if ρ is real-valued then |ρ| = ρ+ + ρ− (the Jordan decomposition). The proof establishes additivity/completeness/regularity of |ρ| and norm properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequality for integrals in total-variation norm
rubrics_metrics.description: For bounded Borel function f and ρ in M(X, C), |∫ f dρ| ≤ ||ρ|| · ||f||_sup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This estimate follows from the definition of the total-variation norm and is used to show that integration against ρ defines a bounded linear functional on C(X) with operator norm ≤ ||ρ||; equality is obtained in the isometric correspondence theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radon–Nikodym type representation for complex measures (existence of density h) (remark in Proposition 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ρ ∈ M(X, C) then (writing ρ in terms of real and imaginary parts) by Radon–Nikodym there exist integrable functions h_R, h_I such that ρR = h_R d|ρ| and ρI = h_I d|ρ|; combine to get a complex Borel function h with |h| = 1 a.e. [d|ρ|] so that dρ = h d|ρ|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence of h (with |h|=1 a.e.) is used to prove the sharp inequality |∫ f dρ| ≤ ||ρ|| ||f||_sup and to relate complex measures to their total variation; a contradiction argument shows |h| must be ≤1 a.e. and normalization yields |h| = 1 a.e.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex-case Riesz correspondence is isometric (Theorem 11.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: The one-one complex-linear map of M(X, C) onto C(X, C)* given by ρ ↦ (f ↦ ∫ f dρ) is norm preserving: the total-variation norm on M(X,C) equals the operator norm on the corresponding functional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses Proposition 11.27 (total-variation properties) and a partition/approximation argument (compact sets Ki, Urysohn-type functions) to construct continuous test functions demonstrating equality of norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Banach space
rubrics_metrics.description: A Banach space is a normed linear space that is complete as a metric space (complete with respect to the metric induced by its norm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness means every Cauchy sequence converges in the space; the metric-space completion of any normed linear space is a Banach space and inherits a compatible norm structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator norm and space of bounded linear operators
rubrics_metrics.description: For a bounded linear operator L : X → Y the operator norm is ||L|| = sup_{||x||≤1} ||L(x)||_Y. The set of bounded linear operators L(X,Y) with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication and this operator norm is a normed linear space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inequalities show ||L1 + L2|| ≤ ||L1|| + ||L2|| and ||cL|| = |c| ||L||. The operator norm is the least M such that ||L(x)|| ≤ M ||x|| for all x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of operator space when range is complete (Proposition 12.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are normed linear spaces and Y is complete, then L(X, Y) (bounded linear operators from X to Y with operator norm) is a Banach space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: any Cauchy sequence of operators is pointwise Cauchy on each x ∈ X; completeness of Y gives pointwise limits which define a linear operator L; uniform boundedness and limiting arguments show L is bounded and the sequence converges to L in operator norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual space X* is a Banach space and norm formula
rubrics_metrics.description: The dual X* (bounded linear functionals on X) is a Banach space. For x* ∈ X* the norm is ||x*|| = sup_{||x||≤1} |x*(x)|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the special case Y = F (scalars) of Proposition 12.1, noting F is complete; the supremum formula characterizes the operator norm for functionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duality of L^p spaces (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under suitable hypotheses (notably σ-finiteness of µ), (L^p(S, µ))^* ≅ L^{p'}(S, µ) via the pairing x*(f) = ∫ f g dµ where p' is the dual exponent with 1/p + 1/p' = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identification gives equality of norms ||x*|| = ||g||_{p'}; the σ-finiteness hypothesis is necessary in general, and the case p=1 or p=∞ requires special attention (counterexamples exist without σ-finiteness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual of C(S) is M(S) via Riesz representation (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: For S compact Hausdorff, C(S)* ≅ M(S) where each bounded linear functional on C(S) corresponds uniquely to a regular Borel signed (or complex) measure ρ and x*(f) = ∫ f dρ; norms match (total-variation norm on M(S) equals operator norm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the content of Theorems 11.26 and 11.28 and was used throughout Section XI to identify measures with functionals on continuous functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of standard examples of Banach spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Common Banach spaces include: Euclidean spaces R^n and C^n; finite-dimensional normed spaces; B(S) (bounded scalar functions with sup norm); C(S) (bounded continuous functions with sup norm); C0(S) (vanishing at infinity); L^p(S, µ) for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ (with completeness hypotheses); sequence spaces c, c0, ℓ^p; M(S) (regular Borel measures with total-variation norm); C^N([a,b]) (functions with bounded derivatives up to order N); H^∞(D) and A(D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item is briefly justified or referenced: completeness results are given earlier in the book (e.g., Theorems and Propositions referenced) and some spaces require additional hypotheses (e.g., measure σ-finiteness for certain dual identifications). These examples serve as standard test-cases in functional analysis.
